setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Uploader says the show shifts into top gear with an incendiary Let It Grow; Features excellent interplay between Garcia and Mydland [3][10][12][13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Reviewer rates the Scarlet-Fire a perfect ten, driven at a pace never matched again in their experience; Strong jam build-ups lead into key points like the Wind in the Willows verse [16][17][19]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): The Fire section ends with a nice, different flow; Garcia gets the lyrics right in both Scarlet and Fire, which is rare [10][17]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opening Minglewood vicious [12]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Brent and Jerry both play standout solos, with Jerry's turns climbing higher and higher [12]

## The recordings

- **gd82-09-11.sbd.clugston.2192.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is good for cassettes from this era; Soundboard flaw: Brent's keyboards overshadow Jerry's solos during Fire; Garcia's guitar drops back during Fire, letting listeners focus on layered drumming and other players [10][13][19]
- **gd1982-09-11.146916.mtx.seamons.ht116.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 171 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Garcia's guitar sits low late in Scarlet-Fire, though the matrix mix helps somewhat; Brief soundboard cut in the Terrapin to Drums transition, three small cuts in One More Saturday Night, plus odd second-set anomalies [3]
- **gd1982-09-11.155686.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 171 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1982-09-11.aud.unknown.85854.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 2.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Level adjustments are distorted during the first minute of Minglewood [5]

## Around the show

- Only appearance at this venue, locally nicknamed Leakey Teepee for its architecture and poor condition [13]
- Reviewer from North Palm Beach meant to see Judas Priest in Ft. Lauderdale, found it sold out, and went elsewhere [15]
- Reviewer's first show; stood right in front of Jerry and felt the band was on [18]
- Crowd was groovy and very cool [20]
- Reviewer's Volvo wagon ran out of gas on I-95 South heading back to Lauderdale [20]
- Reviewer says the Scarlet-Fire pace was never matched again at any other Dead show they saw [16]
- Reviewer prefers this Scarlet>Fire to the one from 9-25-81 at Lehigh U [17]
- Garcia's first-set playing is spectacular and frenetic, unlike a typical 1982 show [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd82-09-11.sbd.clugston.2192.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Master soundboard cassette copied to reel, then DAT, then CDR, with patches from an audience Nak CM300 tape; Scott Clugston circulated it [1]
- **gd1982-09-11.146916.mtx.seamons.ht116.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons [3]
- **gd1982-09-11.155686.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 10, 2022; source: SBD > Cassette Master > DAT (44.1k) [4]. Also: Patch source was pitch-adjusted by 0.7 percent to match the corrected soundboard; patch from Dave Flaschner and Jeff Mitchel, settings by Joe B. Jones [4]
- **gd1982-09-11.aud.unknown.85854.sbeok.flac16**: source: Two AUD cassette sources of unknown lineage [5]. Also: Audience-tape merge: one source covers first set, encore and a Terrapin patch; another source supplies the second set [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-09-11 West Palm Beach Auditorium, West Palm Beach, FL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-09-11-west-palm-beach-auditorium-west-palm-beach-fl-usa/) [22]
